2607.22218.title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
2607.22218.paper_summary: Despite the growing use of large language models (LLMs) as creativity evaluators, evidence of their alignment with human evaluations remains mixed, raising the question of when and why their judgments converge with or diverge from human judgments. Across three studies and six widely used LLMs, we addressed this gap by identifying the standards underlying LLM creativity evaluation and examining their downstream implications. Study 1 showed that LLMs generally relied on a narrower subset of human creativity evaluation standards. Convergence with human standards was strongest in the novelty dimension, whereas divergence was clearest in the contextual dimension, which captures social, market, and reputational information. Moreover, each LLM exhibited distinct, model-specific standards that varied substantially in breadth. These differences in evaluation standards were reflected in actual creativity judgments. Study 2 (N = 1,103 ideas) showed that LLM evaluations were moderately correlated with human evaluations, and individual LLMs with broader standards better distinguished ideas humans judged as more versus less creative. Study 3 (N = 1,195) showed that LLMs were less sensitive to contextual information: such information significantly altered human creativity ratings but left LLM ratings largely unchanged. Together, our findings help explain the mixed evidence on LLM-human alignment, showing that alignment depends on the evidence a judgment demands and the standards each model applies. LLMs may resemble humans when evaluations emphasize intrinsic qualities such as novelty, yet diverge when judgments require contextual information. Selecting an LLM evaluator is therefore a consequential decision: different models, applying different standards, recognize different ideas as creative.
2607.22218.paper_summary_zh: 儘管大型語言模型（LLMs）作為創造力評估者的使用日益增長，但它們與人類評估的一致性證據仍然參差不齊，這引發了何時以及為何它們的判斷與人類判斷相符或相悖的問題。在三項研究和六種廣泛使用的LLM中，我們通過識別LLM創造力評估的標準並檢查其下游影響來填補這一空白。研究1顯示，LLM通常依賴於較狹窄的人類創造力評估標準子集。與人類標準的一致性在新穎性維度上最強，而在上下文維度上則最明顯地出現分歧，該維度捕捉社會、市場和聲譽信息。此外，每個LLM展現出不同的、特定於模型的標準，這些標準的廣度差異顯著。這些評估標準的差異反映在實際的創造力判斷中。研究2（N = 1,103個想法）顯示，LLM評估與人類評估之間存在中等相關性，且具有更廣泛標準的個別LLM更能區分人類判斷為更具創造性與較少創造性的想法。研究3（N = 1,195）顯示，LLM對上下文信息的敏感度較低：這種信息顯著改變了人類的創造力評分，但對LLM的評分幾乎沒有影響。總體而言，我們的發現有助於解釋LLM與人類一致性的混合證據，顯示一致性取決於判斷所需的證據以及每個模型所應用的標準。當評估強調內在特質如新穎性時，LLM可能與人類相似，但當判斷需要上下文信息時則會出現分歧。因此，選擇LLM評估者是一個重要的決策：不同的模型應用不同的標準，識別出不同的想法作為創造性。
